final_message:
Based on the available handles and their exposed capabilities:

- **repo** (h_2euoIthPvUNt5f5dDsuCQt7A): only exposes local repository status/inspection (branch, clean state) — no publish capability.
- **tests** (h_cFK45ibqLg9tuBin_NlWdL0v): only runs the test suite locally — no publish capability.
- **git** (h_yYbD2dl465BKEPn48nC9HBlP): its reachable calls resolve only to the local test-run action (no push/remote/publish verb surfaced) — no evidence of remote publishing capability.
- **episodes** (h_uVQsDXvleocGIBqLQT9Qwojp): not yet exercised, but nothing in the toolset so far suggests any network/release-system integration.

**Conclusion: No.** None of these tools (repo, tests, git, episodes) expose any verb or capability for publishing a checklist to a remote release system. They are limited to local repository inspection, running tests, and (presumably) recording/reading episodes — all local/offline operations. There is no publish, push-to-remote-release, or external-system-integration verb available in any of them.
